## What's new

Threadnote 4 beta.30 makes native code-graph indexing more predictable on large monorepos with generated output, heavy TypeScript, and large test artifacts.

- Code extraction now runs in a bounded worker pool shared across concurrent Threadnote processes and feeds one
  backpressured SQLite writer. A parser timeout, crash, or malformed response degrades only that file to searchable
  metadata; later indexing can retry it instead of retaining a transient failure.
- Interactive `threadnote graph index` output now identifies Git read batches, the current file and language with parse
  timing, and SQLite persistence batches. Structured `--json` progress is streamed on stderr so the final stdout
  document remains parseable, while Manager shows the same privacy-safe stage and timing information.
- Recognized snapshots, golden files, fixtures, datasets, test data, and animation JSON/YAML are
  streaming-fingerprinted and represented as file/module metadata without hydrating their payloads. Large unknown JSON,
  JSONC, and YAML use bounded or shallow extraction; manifests, schemas, and configuration files retain their dedicated
  graph extraction.
- Hidden directories and conventional generated roots—including `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `out`, `.nx`,
  coverage output, and `bazel-*`—are pruned before content reads, even below broad monorepo package roots. Binary media
  remains metadata-only and textless SVGs avoid unnecessary parsing.
- Pathological TypeScript keeps imports, exports, declarations, and inheritance after dynamic call traversal reaches
  its per-file complexity budget. Repeated identical call evidence is deduplicated before it reaches the parser cache
  without changing final graph topology.
- A new Bazel/Starlark language pack indexes `WORKSPACE*`, `MODULE.bazel`, `BUILD*`, `.bzl`, and `.bazelrc` declarations,
  targets, loads, calls, configuration, and labels. Nested Bazel workspaces and apps integrated into an outer monorepo
  are modeled statically; Threadnote never invokes Bazel or evaluates macros.
- Extractor generation 10 performs one clean graph rebuild after update so older eligibility and extraction facts
  cannot remain active. Completed parser-cache batches remain reusable after interruption, and single-worker, parallel,
  and interrupted/resumed builds are checked for deterministic output.
- The stored 4,269-file heavy-tail fixture covers call-heavy and generated TypeScript, a 25 MiB snapshot, and 4,000
  textless SVGs. It completed without parser degradation and produced the same graph digest in one-worker, four-worker,
  and resumed runs; on the recorded M1 Max run, fact deduplication made the parser cache 86.5% smaller and reduced peak
  RSS by 38–43%. These measurements are a same-machine regression reference, not a portable latency gate.
- New integration, property-based, and scheduled benchmark coverage exercises per-file budgets, Bazel/Starlark
  extraction, source spans, interruption/resume, deterministic parallel extraction, structured progress, and
  large-monorepo heavy tails.

Existing beta installations can update in place:

```bash
threadnote update --beta
```

Fresh beta installation:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kashkovsky/threadnote/v4.0.0-beta.30/scripts/install.sh |
  sh -s -- --beta
```
